Most of these mistakes are just stylistic, or errors of judgement on minor points. The fatal error in writing a novel is being unable to carry it through from the promises it makes in the beginning. I can't even number the novels I've read that started out with an interesting premise, and then just petered out and came to nothing. Follow-through is the killer in literature. A great novel is one that builds and builds and builds and then delivers. Unless it does this it never manages to come alive in the mind of the reader. It always comes across as contrived or forced or stiff or mechanical. I'd almost go so far as to say that it doesn't matter what a novelist chooses to write about, as long as he delivers on his promises and makes his work come alive for his readers.
